title: Chrome browser profiles
whyItMatters: Each profile is a separate browsing identity. Profile names and the accounts signed into Chrome show who used this computer and how many separated identities they kept.
source: Chromium docs, user data directory and per-profile folders; Chrome on Linux keeps its user data root in ~/.config/google-chrome: https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/docs/user_data_dir.md
notes: Matches the Preferences file that every profile has, so sibling non-profile folders are skipped. google-chrome is the stable package; beta and dev use google-chrome-beta and google-chrome-unstable. The Local State file with the profile list sits next to the profile folders.

cleanup.exportFirst: In Chrome, export your passwords from the password manager and your bookmarks from the bookmark manager, and save both files off this computer.
cleanup.signOut: In Chrome, open Settings > You and Google and turn sync off or sign out, so the account keeps the synced data but this browser stops using it.
steps: Uninstall Google Chrome from the App Center if you are removing the browser itself.
Move the profile folder that holds the file named in the plan to the Trash, then empty the Trash.
cleanup.risk: Removes every Chrome profile on this computer: history, bookmarks, saved passwords, cookies, extensions and open sessions.
cleanup.source: Google Chrome Help, Sign in and turn on sync in Chrome: https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/185277
